findings.issue_text: [BUG] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService's signature changes (anonStore anonstore.AnonStore swapped for sqlStore db.DB) but the wire-generated caller in wire_gen.go is not regenerated in this diff, so the Go build breaks with a compile error on the old positional arguments. The repo does not compile until wire_gen.go is regenerated; CI fails immediately, and no reviewer instruction in the diff notes the required wire regen.

[BUG] impl.go imports "github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/infra/db" while anonstore/database.go's ProvideAnonDBStore takes db.DB from "github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/services/sqlstore/db"; infra/db.DB is a concrete wrapper struct, not the sqlstore db.DB interface, so the wire graph's *sqlstore.SQLStore cannot be injected into the new sqlStore db.DB parameter. Wire generation fails or wire_gen cannot satisfy the new parameter with the existing sqlstore provider, breaking the build that the diff assumes still works with the old dependency wiring.

[BUG] GrafanaBootConfig declares anonymousDeviceLimit and the backend DTO emits anonymousDeviceLimit, but no code in this diff maps the /frontend/settings DTO value into GrafanaBootConfig, so the frontend field stays undefined regardless of the ini setting. Any frontend consumer reading config.anonymousDeviceLimit (the presumed reason for the type change in grafana-data/grafana-runtime) always reads undefined even when device_limit is configured, silently shipping a dead config surface.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice is built on dbSession.Exec(args...) with the query prepended into the variadic args, and relies on CountDevices existing in the AnonStore interface, which this diff does not show being added or verified. If CountDevices is not already present on AnonStore (the diff modifies the interface file without touching the AnonStore interface declaration), the package does not compile; a staff reviewer should confirm the symbol exists before merge.

[BUG] TagDevice now returns tagDeviceUI errors, so any transient database failure while tagging a device fails the entire anonymous authentication instead of degrading gracefully. Anonymous users lose access to Grafana whenever the anon_device write fails (DB blip, lock timeout), converting a previously non-blocking telemetry write into an authentication-availability dependency; previously the error was logged and auth proceeded.

[BUG] Authenticate returns the raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached with no mapping to a user-facing response, so anonymous clients beyond the limit get an opaque authentication failure (401/500) instead of any defined UX. Once the device limit is reached, every new anonymous visitor receives an internal error page with no explanation; the diff defines no HTTP mapping, no 429-style response, and no frontend message for this state, and no test verifies what an over-limit request actually returns.

[BUG] The count-then-act check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is not atomic, so concurrent first-seen devices can all pass the count check and exceed deviceLimit. Under concurrent traffic (exactly the scenario a device limit targets, e.g. a scraping fleet), N simultaneous requests each read count < limit and insert, blowing past the configured cap; the limit is advisory, not enforced, contradicting the feature's acceptance criteria.

[ADVISORY] The goroutine+timeout wrapper around TagDevice was removed, making device tagging a synchronous DB round-trip inline in the anonymous authentication hot path. Every anonymous request on a local-cache miss now pays authentication latency for the device write (and, when deviceLimit > 0, an extra COUNT query in CreateOrUpdateDevice); a slow or loaded database directly slows anonymous page loads, which the previous fire-and-forget design deliberately isolated.

[ADVISORY] The new test only covers the limit-rejected path; the core behavior that an existing device at the limit still updates successfully (rowsAffected > 0 branch of updateDevice) has no test in this diff. A regression in the updateDevice WHERE clause or args (e.g. the BETWEEN window) that makes every over-limit update fail would return ErrDeviceLimitReached for all returning anonymous devices, locking out the entire existing user base — and the current test suite would stay green.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceLimit is plumbed into the frontend boot config but no code in this diff consumes it, and the Go DTO always serializes a number (0 by default) while the TS type claims number | undefined. Frontend code keying off `=== undefined` (the type's promise) never matches because backend always sends 0, and the exposed setting is currently inert — operators can set device_limit but the UI offers no feedback that the limit was hit, consistent with the opaque 401/500 behavior on the backend.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's BETWEEN window is computed from device.UpdatedAt (request time) rather than a clock read at execution time, coupling the expiry predicate to the caller-supplied timestamp. Any future caller that passes a backdated or client-influenced UpdatedAt silently widens or shifts the 30-day match window, and the same 30-day expiration constant is now duplicated between the count window, the update window, and the API's ListDevices fromTime — three sites that must be updated in lockstep on the next change.

[BUG] When the device limit is reached, Authenticate returns an error, which fails the entire anonymous authentication instead of only declining to tag a new device. Every anonymous request from an unseen device gets a failed authentication (and likely an error response) once the limit is hit; existing devices keep working only via updateDevice, so all new visitors are locked out of the instance with an opaque internal error — a denial-of-service vector where any third party can pre-claim device IDs up to the limit. Enforcing the limit belongs in the device-tagging path, not by failing authn.

[ADVISORY] The diff replaces asynchronous, panic-recovered, timeout-bounded device tagging with a synchronous inline call on the authentication hot path — work not required by 'add a configurable device limit'. Every anonymous authentication now blocks on a DB count query plus write (CreateOrUpdateDevice/CountDevices) before returning an identity, adding per-request DB latency and coupling authn availability to anonstore availability; previously a tagging failure or panic could not slow or fail authn. Even if needed to surface ErrDeviceLimitReached, the removal of the timeout and panic recovery is unexplained scope expansion.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceLimit is added to the public frontend settings payload and all three frontend config types, but no frontend code in this diff consumes it. Ships-inert surface expansion: an internal server-side enforcement knob is exposed to every browser (and to anonymous unauthenticated users via /api/frontend-settings), leaking configuration detail with no consumer; the TS type number|undefined never receives undefined since the Go DTO serializes int64 zero-value as 0, so the 'unset' representation is also inconsistent.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice silently changes from swallowing tagDeviceUI errors to propagating them, a behavior change unrelated to the device-limit feature. Any transient store error during device tagging now propagates to callers that previously saw nil; combined with client.go no longer logging-and-continuing for non-limit errors, a flaky anon_device table turns previously-tolerated tagging hiccups into authn-path errors. Not traceable to the device-limit requirement.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService drops the injected anonStore.AnonStore dependency and constructs AnonDBStore inline, breaking the existing DI seam. The anonStore parameter is removed from the constructor signature, so tests and alternative implementations (e.g. the existing AnonStore interface abstraction) can no longer inject a fake store; the next change to the store (or anyone extending AnonStore) must now construct a real DB. The abstraction AnonStore remains in the interface but its injection point is deleted — under-scoped refactor bundled into the feature.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration (30*24*time.Hour) is duplicated in two packages — anonstore/database.go and anonimpl/api/api.go — as parallel hand-maintained constants that were previously one shared constant. If the retention window ever diverges from the device-listing window, the limit's count window and the admin device-list window disagree silently; the api package previously defined thirtyDays and this diff renames it locally instead of extracting a shared constant in anonstore (where it is now first-class).

[BUG] The limit enforcement is a check-then-insert (COUNT, then either INSERT or UPDATE) with no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint, so two concurrent anonymous requests both observe count < limit and both insert. Under any concurrency (which is the norm for anonymous traffic), the device table exceeds the configured limit the moment two first-seen devices race; the limit is only approximately enforced and drifts upward over time since nothing ever evicts to re-enforce it.

[BUG] updateDevice treats rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached, but rowsAffected==0 also occurs when the device row exists yet its stored updated_at falls outside the BETWEEN window (updated_at > 30 days old or clock skew beyond +1 minute), conflating 'device is stale/expired' with 'device does not exist'. A known returning device whose stored updated_at has aged past the window is refused with ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being refreshed, and because CountDevices counts only rows within the window (time.Now-based) while updateDevice's window is anchored on device.UpdatedAt, a device can be counted against the limit yet still fail the UPDATE predicate — the user is locked out and no slot is freed by their return.

[BUG] Sentinel-meaning change: TagDevice errors now propagate synchronously from Authenticate, and only the ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel is returned to the authn layer — every other tag failure path also became synchronous and DB-failure-dependent, where previously the goroutine guaranteed authentication never depended on device tagging at all. An anonymous device store outage (or slow DB) now blocks/slow every anonymous authentication on the hot path instead of being logged and ignored; a degraded anon-device backend degrades all anonymous access rather than degrading device tracking.

[ADVISORY] When deviceLimit > 0, every anonymous request now issues an extra synchronous COUNT over the 30-day anon_device window before the upsert, doubling the DB round-trips on the authentication hot path, and the query's updated_at range predicate relies on an index on updated_at that this diff neither adds nor verifies. Every anonymous page load pays two DB queries (COUNT + UPDATE/INSERT) where one sufficed, and on a large anon_device table without an updated_at index the COUNT is a full scan per request — a scalability cliff exactly where the limit is configured (large anonymous deployments).

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration (30*24*time.Hour) is now duplicated as an identical constant in two packages (anonstore/database.go and anonimpl/api.go), replacing the previously shared thirtyDays with parallel hand-maintained copies. The device-limit window and the ListDevices window are semantically the same retention period but have no single source of truth; the next change to retention (e.g. 30d -> 7d) edits one file and silently makes the limit window disagree with the UI/API window, miscounting which devices count against the limit.

[ADVISORY] The Go DTO exposes AnonymousDeviceLimit as a plain int64 with no omitempty, so disabled (0) is serialized as 0, while the TS side models it as number | undefined and the runtime default is undefined — the two sides disagree on how 'no limit' is represented across the process boundary. Frontend code branching on undefined ('not configured') never sees it from the Go backend (always a number), and a frontend that treats 0 as 'limit of zero devices' rather than 'unlimited' misbehaves for every default-config deployment; the sentinel semantics are split between two type systems with no documented mapping.

[ADVISORY] device_limit is read with MustInt64 and consumed only via s.deviceLimit > 0, so negative values and the 0 default are silently equivalent to 'unlimited' with no validation or warning. An operator who sets device_limit = -1 (or makes a typo like device_limit = 1OO resolved to 0) gets unlimited anonymous devices with no log line, believing a limit is in force — the misconfiguration is invisible until the table grows unbounded.

[BUG] When the device limit is reached, Authenticate returns (nil, ErrDeviceLimitReached), which fails the entire anonymous authentication instead of merely skipping device tagging, so every anonymous request from a new device is rejected once the limit is hit. Once device_limit is reached, all not-yet-seen anonymous devices get authentication errors on every request — the original intent was to cap tracked devices, not to deny anonymous access; the objective silently changed from 'limit device records' to 'lock out anonymous users' without human acceptance.

[BUG] TagDevice now propagates tagDeviceUI errors (added 'return err') where it previously logged the failure and returned nil, so transient DB/cache failures now fail anonymous authentication. Any error from tagDeviceUI (DB blip, cache error) now turns into a failed anonymous authn request; previously such failures were degraded gracefully with a log line — a behavior change slipped in under a 'configurable device limit' PR.

[ADVISORY] Device tagging was silently converted from a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout and panic recovery to a synchronous inline call on the request path. Every anonymous request now pays the latency of a CountDevices query (and updateDevice insert) inline — a hot-path regression where a slow/degraded anonstore database directly delays all anonymous page loads, and a panic in TagDevice previously recovered no longer is contained.

[BUG] updateDevice's WHERE clause requires the existing device's updated_at to be within the 30-day window, so a known device whose row is older than 30 days gets ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being refreshed, permanently locking that returning device out even though it is a repeat visitor. A returning anonymous device with a stale row (e.g., rows not purged yet, or CreatedAt but stale updated_at) is treated as a new device and rejected every time; the device can never be re-admitted until DeleteDevicesOlderThan runs, defeating the intent of counting distinct devices.

[ADVISORY] The count-then-update limit check is a TOCTOU race: concurrent requests can each observe count < limit and insert, exceeding device_limit. Under concurrent anonymous traffic the limit is only approximate; operators configuring an exact cap get more devices than configured — acceptable if documented, but the config option reads as an exact guarantee.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts the injected anonStore.AnonStore and instead constructs AnonDBStore internally, removing the DI seam. Out-of-tree/enterprise code that injected a custom AnonStore implementation (e.g., a remote device store) silently stops being used; this is a public-surface change hidden inside a feature PR.

[ADVISORY] The frontend type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined but the Go DTO serializes it as int64 with zero value 0, so the frontend can never observe 'undefined' and cannot distinguish 'unlimited' from a real limit of 0. Frontend code written against the declared type will treat the always-present 0 as a real value; anyone building UI/API surfacing on this field must know 0 means unset, a contract mismatch baked in at type level.

[BUG] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit reuses the same Device struct and mutates DeviceID after the first insert, but the first device was inserted with UpdatedAt one hour in the past while the test's limit check counts devices within the 30-day window — the test only exercises the count>=limit path, never verifying that an existing device within the window can still be updated. The update path for an existing device when the limit is reached (the core intended behavior of the feature) has no coverage; a regression in the UPDATE matching would pass CI and lock out all returning devices in production.

[BUG] The device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices and then performs the upsert as two separate statements with no transaction or row lock, so concurrent anonymous requests all observe count < deviceLimit and each insert a new device row. Under concurrent load the configured device limit is exceeded (limit is advisory, not enforced), and conversely once near the limit concurrent requests race to return ErrDeviceLimitReached for devices that would have fit; an attacker driving parallel requests with rotating cookies can overshoot the operator's cap.

[BUG] ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned from Authenticate as an authentication error, so anonymous requests from new devices surface as a generic auth failure (likely HTTP 500 from the authn pipeline) rather than a defined 4xx/redirect response, and the previously fire-and-forget tagging path is now a blocking failure point on every anonymous request. A transient count-query failure no longer degrades gracefully (that path is still logged), but the limit-reached path turns routine anonymous browsing into hard auth errors with no client-visible contract; any operator setting device_limit locks out all new anonymous visitors with server errors.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE window is computed from device.UpdatedAt while the limit decision in CreateOrUpdateDevice uses time.Now(), so a device whose stored updated_at is older than 30 days cannot be updated (BETWEEN excludes it) even though CountDevices' now-based window may not count it, leaving a device unable to be created or refreshed until the row is garbage-collected. A returning anonymous device whose row is stale gets ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever the limit is active and the count is at/over the cap, even if the count is inflated only by rows that are themselves outside the update window — users see intermittent lockouts that the operator cannot explain.

[ADVISORY] device_limit is read from config as an unvalidated int64 with no upper bound, and the enforcement stores the raw value in AnonDBStore without clamping, so a typo'd or adversarially huge config value (e.g. 9223372036854775807) is silently accepted while a large-but-real value is fine — no sanity check at parse time. Operators get no feedback on misconfiguration; the effective behavior (unlimited via 0 default) silently applies for any non-positive value including negatives, which differs from what a reader of the config key expects.

[ADVISORY] ErrDeviceLimitReached is defined inside the anonstore package and detected by errors.Is across package boundaries in client.go, but nothing in the diff documents or translates it at the HTTP layer, leaving a sentinel error from the storage layer as the user-facing auth outcome. Future refactors that wrap or re-create the error (fmt.Errorf without %w) silently convert a 'deny new device' outcome into a generic anonymous-auth failure logged as a warning, changing availability behavior with no compile-time signal.

[BUG] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only exercises the limit-rejection path and never tests the 'at-limit device is updated instead of rejected' success path of the new updateDevice branch. updateDevice's success path (rowsAffected > 0, existing device refreshed when at the limit — the entire point of the feature per the comment 'if device limit is reached, only update devices') has zero coverage; a regression in the UPDATE's WHERE clause (e.g. updated_at window computed wrong so legitimate devices are always rejected) would pass CI, silently locking out returning anonymous users while the test suite stays green.

[BUG] TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag constructs the service via setting.NewCfg() (AnonymousDeviceLimit=0) and asserts only require.NoError, so the new synchronous error propagation in TagDevice (the diff-changed 'return err' on tagDeviceUI failure) and the limit enforcement path are never triggered by any test in this diff. TagDevice's behavior changed from swallowing tagDeviceUI errors to returning them, and the new device-limit plumbing flows through ProvideAnonymousDeviceService, but the only existing caller-level tests assert the happy path with limit 0 — an error-return regression or a wrong limit value wired into ProvideAnonDBStore would pass the suite.

[ADVISORY] The new ErrDeviceLimitReached short-circuit in Anonymous.Authenticate (returning nil, err so anonymous authentication fails) has no test in the diff's test files (database_test.go, impl_test.go), and the async-to-sync change removing the goroutine/timeout is likewise unverified. This is a user-visible auth behavior change (anonymous users get rejected at the limit); a regression here — e.g. the errors.Is check failing to match a wrapped error so every anonymous request errors, or conversely the error never propagating — would ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit reuses one Device struct and leaves CreatedAt unset, so the first row is inserted with the zero time while UpdatedAt is now-1h. The test's data shape diverges from real callers (which set both timestamps); assertions keyed on timestamp windows (the BETWEEN updated_at-30d AND updated_at+1m predicate) are validated against inconsistent seed data, weakening confidence in the window logic the test claims to exercise.

[BUG] A device whose stored updated_at is older than 30 days can never be updated once the limit is reached, because the UPDATE's `updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt-30d AND device.UpdatedAt+1m` window excludes it, RowsAffected returns 0, and the store permanently returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for that device. A returning anonymous user whose device row was last touched >30 days ago (it then stops being counted by CountDevices' 30-day window, so the limit appears to have room, yet the row still exists) is locked out forever: every request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and the row can never be refreshed back into the counted window.

[BUG] The limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices and then performs the INSERT outside any transaction or lock, so concurrent requests all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert. With N concurrent first-time devices, the device count exceeds the configured limit (classic TOCTOU), silently defeating the limit the feature exists to enforce; no error or partial state is surfaced.

[ADVISORY] Authenticate now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached as an authentication error, converting what was previously fire-and-forget device tagging into an authn failure that denies anonymous access to brand-new devices. Once the limit is reached, every new device gets an authentication failure (surfacing 'device limit reached' as the auth error) rather than anonymous access with an untagged device — a user-visible behavior change from the previous design where tagging failures never blocked authentication; if blocking is intended, the error message presented to end users is raw and unhelpful.

[ADVISORY] AnonymousDeviceLimit is added to FrontendSettingsDTO and GrafanaBootConfig but no code in this diff reads it on the frontend, and the TS default `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` never matches the Go serialization, which always emits the JSON number 0 for the unset case. Ships-inert frontend surface: the config field is broadcast to every browser on every page load carrying no consumer, and the `number | undefined` type misdescribes the actual wire shape (always a number, 0 meaning unset), so future frontend code checking truthiness will treat a legitimate limit of 0 (disabled) and 'absent' identically only by accident.

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

The repo does not compile until wire_gen.go is regenerated; CI fails immediately, and no reviewer instruction in the diff notes the required wire regen.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` to accept `sqlStore db.DB` instead of `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` (in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go`), and updates some call sites in tests accordingly. However, the diff does not show any updates to potential DI/wire-generated call sites (e.g., `wire_gen.go`). If such a file exists and still calls the old signature positionally, it would cause a compile-time error until regenerated/updated. This is a build-breaking defect, though the actual `wire_gen.go` usage is not visible in the provided diff.

Wire generation fails or wire_gen cannot satisfy the new parameter with the existing sqlstore provider, breaking the build that the diff assumes still works with the old dependency wiring.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` in `impl.go` now takes `sqlStore db.DB` where `db` is imported from `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/infra/db`, and then passes that value into `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, ...)`. In `anonstore/database.go`, `ProvideAnonDBStore` accepts `sqlStore db.DB` and the implementation uses `sqlstore.DBSession` (`s.sqlStore.WithDbSession(... *sqlstore.DBSession ...)`), strongly implying this `db.DB` is the sqlstore DB abstraction (i.e., from `pkg/services/sqlstore/db`), not `infra/db`. If these `db.DB` types are from different packages (as the finding states), this change would introduce a compile-time/type mismatch and break DI/wire generation/build. The mismatch is not explicitly visible in the `database.go` imports in the diff, so the exact package can’t be 100% confirmed from the snippet, but the evidence points to it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GrafanaBootConfig declares anonymousDeviceLimit and the backend DTO emits anonymousDeviceLimit, but no code in this diff maps the /frontend/settings DTO value into GrafanaBootConfig, so the frontend field stays undefined regardless of the ini setting. Any frontend consumer reading config.anonymousDeviceLimit (the presumed reason for the type change in grafana-data/grafana-runtime) always reads undefined even when device_limit is configured, silently shipping a dead config surface.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `anonymousDeviceLimit` to the backend `/frontend/settings` DTO and adds a corresponding field/default (`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined`) to `GrafanaBootConfig`, but the diff does not show the code path that hydrates `GrafanaBootConfig` from the boot payload. That mapping could already be generic (e.g., `Object.assign`/spread from the JSON) and unchanged, in which case the field would not stay `undefined`. Since the hydration/mapping logic is not present in this diff, the claim that the frontend will “always read undefined regardless of the ini setting” is not verifiable from the diff alone.

If CountDevices is not already present on AnonStore (the diff modifies the interface file without touching the AnonStore interface declaration), the package does not compile; a staff reviewer should confirm the symbol exists before merge.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s compilation claim about `CountDevices` depending on the `AnonStore` interface is not supported by the diff: `CountDevices` is invoked as `s.CountDevices(...)` on the concrete receiver `*AnonDBStore` inside `database.go`, not via an `AnonStore`-typed value, so the interface need not include it for this code to compile. The other concern about `dbSession.Exec(args...)` with the query prepended cannot be verified from the diff alone because the signature/behavior of `sqlstore.DBSession.Exec` is not shown (this “query as first variadic arg” pattern may be valid in this codebase).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TagDevice now returns tagDeviceUI errors, so any transient database failure while tagging a device fails the entire anonymous authentication instead of degrading gracefully. Anonymous users lose access to Grafana whenever the anon_device write fails (DB blip, lock timeout), converting a previously non-blocking telemetry write into an authentication-availability dependency; previously the error was logged and auth proceeded.

adjudication.rationale: While TagDevice now returns the error from tagDeviceUI (impl.go: TagDevice now does `return err` after logging), anonymous authentication does not fail on those errors in the updated call site. In client.go Authenticate, the TagDevice call is synchronous, but on any error it only aborts authentication if `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`; all other errors are logged and auth proceeds (`a.log.Warn(...)` then returns an Anonymous identity). Therefore transient DB/tagging failures do not, per this diff, block anonymous users from accessing Grafana (only the explicit device-limit condition does).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Authenticate returns the raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached with no mapping to a user-facing response, so anonymous clients beyond the limit get an opaque authentication failure (401/500) instead of any defined UX. Once the device limit is reached, every new anonymous visitor receives an internal error page with no explanation; the diff defines no HTTP mapping, no 429-style response, and no frontend message for this state, and no test verifies what an over-limit request actually returns.

[BUG] The count-then-act check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is not atomic, so concurrent first-seen devices can all pass the count check and exceed deviceLimit. Under concurrent traffic (exactly the scenario a device limit targets, e.g. a scraping fleet), N simultaneous requests each read count < limit and insert, blowing past the configured cap; the limit is advisory, not enforced, contradicting the feature's acceptance criteria.
matched_golden_ids: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same race condition: a non-atomic count-then-insert check in CreateOrUpdateDevice allows concurrent requests to all pass the device count check and create devices beyond the limit, implying the need for transactional/locking enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The goroutine+timeout wrapper around TagDevice was removed, making device tagging a synchronous DB round-trip inline in the anonymous authentication hot path. Every anonymous request on a local-cache miss now pays authentication latency for the device write (and, when deviceLimit > 0, an extra COUNT query in CreateOrUpdateDevice); a slow or loaded database directly slows anonymous page loads, which the previous fire-and-forget design deliberately isolated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the asynchronous fire-and-forget goroutine in `Anonymous.Authenticate` and replaces it with an inline call: `if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, ...)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). `TagDevice` ultimately persists via the DB-backed anon store; additionally, when `deviceLimit > 0`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` performs a `CountDevices(...)` before potentially updating (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). This makes tagging part of the authentication request path on local-cache misses and can add latency under DB slowness/load, which is an architecture/performance concern grounded in the change, not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new test only covers the limit-rejected path; the core behavior that an existing device at the limit still updates successfully (rowsAffected > 0 branch of updateDevice) has no test in this diff. A regression in the updateDevice WHERE clause or args (e.g. the BETWEEN window) that makes every over-limit update fail would return ErrDeviceLimitReached for all returning anonymous devices, locking out the entire existing user base — and the current test suite would stay green.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds new over-limit logic in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` that calls `s.updateDevice(...)` when `count >= s.deviceLimit` (database.go). `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `rowsAffected == 0`, and succeeds only when an existing device row matches the `WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` clause. The newly added test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` (database_test.go) only asserts the failure path (second, different DeviceID returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`) and does not cover the success path where the limit is reached but an existing device is updated (rowsAffected > 0). Thus a regression in the `WHERE ... BETWEEN ...` window/args could cause all over-limit updates to fail without any test catching it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceLimit is plumbed into the frontend boot config but no code in this diff consumes it, and the Go DTO always serializes a number (0 by default) while the TS type claims number | undefined. Frontend code keying off `=== undefined` (the type's promise) never matches because backend always sends 0, and the exposed setting is currently inert — operators can set device_limit but the UI offers no feedback that the limit was hit, consistent with the opaque 401/500 behavior on the backend.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s core claim that `anonymousDeviceLimit` is “inert” / “no code in this diff consumes it” is contradicted by the diff: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now constructs the store with `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)`, and `CreateOrUpdateDevice` enforces `s.deviceLimit` (counting devices and returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). While there is a verifiable TS/Go shape mismatch (`anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` vs Go `int64` always serialized, defaulting to 0), the finding’s asserted frontend behavior (`=== undefined` checks) and “UI offers no feedback/opaque 401/500” are not shown in this diff and cannot be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] updateDevice's BETWEEN window is computed from device.UpdatedAt (request time) rather than a clock read at execution time, coupling the expiry predicate to the caller-supplied timestamp. Any future caller that passes a backdated or client-influenced UpdatedAt silently widens or shifts the 30-day match window, and the same 30-day expiration constant is now duplicated between the count window, the update window, and the API's ListDevices fromTime — three sites that must be updated in lockstep on the next change.

[BUG] When the device limit is reached, Authenticate returns an error, which fails the entire anonymous authentication instead of only declining to tag a new device. Every anonymous request from an unseen device gets a failed authentication (and likely an error response) once the limit is hit; existing devices keep working only via updateDevice, so all new visitors are locked out of the instance with an opaque internal error — a denial-of-service vector where any third party can pre-claim device IDs up to the limit. Enforcing the limit belongs in the device-tagging path, not by failing authn.

[ADVISORY] The diff replaces asynchronous, panic-recovered, timeout-bounded device tagging with a synchronous inline call on the authentication hot path — work not required by 'add a configurable device limit'. Every anonymous authentication now blocks on a DB count query plus write (CreateOrUpdateDevice/CountDevices) before returning an identity, adding per-request DB latency and coupling authn availability to anonstore availability; previously a tagging failure or panic could not slow or fail authn. Even if needed to surface ErrDeviceLimitReached, the removal of the timeout and panic recovery is unexplained scope expansion.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace the previous goroutine-based, panic-recovered, timeout-bounded tagging in `Anonymous.Authenticate` with a synchronous inline call: the whole `go func(){ ... context.WithTimeout(...); ... recover() ... }()` block is removed and replaced by `if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, ...)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). `TagDevice` now can return an error (impl.go adds `return err` on UI tagging failure), and the new device-limit path does extra DB work (`CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls `CountDevices` and then does an UPDATE/INSERT in anonstore/database.go). While non-limit tagging errors are still only logged (auth continues), the request now blocks on anonstore/DB latency and no longer has the explicit timeout/panic isolation that previously prevented tagging issues from impacting the auth hot path. This is a concrete scope/perf/availability concern grounded in the diff, not a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

Ships-inert surface expansion: an internal server-side enforcement knob is exposed to every browser (and to anonymous unauthenticated users via /api/frontend-settings), leaking configuration detail with no consumer; the TS type number|undefined never receives undefined since the Go DTO serializes int64 zero-value as 0, so the 'unset' representation is also inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds `AnonymousDeviceLimit` to the backend `/api/frontend-settings` payload (`FrontendSettingsDTO` + `getFrontendSettings`) and to the public TS config types (`GrafanaConfig`, `GrafanaBootConfig`), but there is no frontend-side usage shown anywhere in this diff. That’s a concrete surface-area expansion (value sent to every browser, including anonymous users) without an in-diff consumer. The representation mismatch is also verifiable: Go serializes an `int64` field with no `omitempty`, so it will always be present (default `0`), while TS models it as `number | undefined` and initializes it to `undefined` in `GrafanaBootConfig`—so “unset” as `undefined` is inconsistent with what this DTO will emit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TagDevice silently changes from swallowing tagDeviceUI errors to propagating them, a behavior change unrelated to the device-limit feature. Any transient store error during device tagging now propagates to callers that previously saw nil; combined with client.go no longer logging-and-continuing for non-limit errors, a flaky anon_device table turns previously-tolerated tagging hiccups into authn-path errors. Not traceable to the device-limit requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real behavior change in `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice`: it now returns the error from `tagDeviceUI` (`impl.go`: added `return err` inside the `if err != nil` block), whereas previously it logged and then returned `nil`. That change is broader than just propagating `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and could affect any direct callers of `TagDevice` that previously assumed tagging failures were non-fatal. However, the finding’s claim that `client.go` “no longer logging-and-continuing for non-limit errors” is not supported: `Authenticate` still logs a warning and continues for non-limit errors, only returning an error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService drops the injected anonStore.AnonStore dependency and constructs AnonDBStore inline, breaking the existing DI seam. The anonStore parameter is removed from the constructor signature, so tests and alternative implementations (e.g. the existing AnonStore interface abstraction) can no longer inject a fake store; the next change to the store (or anyone extending AnonStore) must now construct a real DB. The abstraction AnonStore remains in the interface but its injection point is deleted — under-scoped refactor bundled into the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed its signature from taking an injected `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to taking `sqlStore db.DB` and then constructing the concrete store internally: `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go). Tests were updated accordingly to pass a real DB store (impl_test.go), confirming the injection seam for alternative/fake `AnonStore` implementations is removed even though the `AnonStore` interface still exists (database.go). This is an architecture/DI regression rather than a direct functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration (30*24*time.Hour) is duplicated in two packages — anonstore/database.go and anonimpl/api/api.go — as parallel hand-maintained constants that were previously one shared constant. If the retention window ever diverges from the device-listing window, the limit's count window and the admin device-list window disagree silently; the api package previously defined thirtyDays and this diff renames it locally instead of extracting a shared constant in anonstore (where it is now first-class).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `const anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour` in two separate places: `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` (used for limit/count/update window) and `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go` (used for ListDevices `fromTime`). These are hand-maintained parallel constants with the same value today, so it’s not a current defect, but it is a real maintainability/architecture risk: if either constant changes independently, the store’s limit/count window and the API’s listing window can diverge silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The limit enforcement is a check-then-insert (COUNT, then either INSERT or UPDATE) with no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint, so two concurrent anonymous requests both observe count < limit and both insert. Under any concurrency (which is the norm for anonymous traffic), the device table exceeds the configured limit the moment two first-seen devices race; the limit is only approximately enforced and drifts upward over time since nothing ever evicts to re-enforce it.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` the new limit logic does `CountDevices(...)` and, if `count < s.deviceLimit`, proceeds to insert/upsert without any transaction, lock, or DB-enforced constraint (`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`). Under concurrent first-seen devices, multiple goroutines can observe `count < limit` and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. Nothing in the diff adds a mechanism to prevent this race or to re-enforce the cap after the fact, so the finding is grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateDevice treats rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached, but rowsAffected==0 also occurs when the device row exists yet its stored updated_at falls outside the BETWEEN window (updated_at > 30 days old or clock skew beyond +1 minute), conflating 'device is stale/expired' with 'device does not exist'. A known returning device whose stored updated_at has aged past the window is refused with ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being refreshed, and because CountDevices counts only rows within the window (time.Now-based) while updateDevice's window is anchored on device.UpdatedAt, a device can be counted against the limit yet still fail the UPDATE predicate — the user is locked out and no slot is freed by their return.
matched_golden_ids: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that updateDevice incorrectly maps rowsAffected==0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached. The candidate explains that zero rows can mean the device doesn't match the UPDATE predicate (missing or outside the time window), not that a limit was reached, which is the same underlying bug described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Sentinel-meaning change: TagDevice errors now propagate synchronously from Authenticate, and only the ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel is returned to the authn layer — every other tag failure path also became synchronous and DB-failure-dependent, where previously the goroutine guaranteed authentication never depended on device tagging at all. An anonymous device store outage (or slow DB) now blocks/slow every anonymous authentication on the hot path instead of being logged and ignored; a degraded anon-device backend degrades all anonymous access rather than degrading device tracking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the goroutine + background timeout in `Anonymous.Authenticate` and calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously instead (client.go). Additionally, `TagDevice` now returns the `tagDeviceUI` error (impl.go adds `return err`), whereas previously it only logged and returned nil. Even though `Authenticate` only *fails* authentication for `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the synchronous call means anonymous authentication is now latency/availability-dependent on the anon-device tagging path (DB/cache) on the hot path, rather than being best-effort and non-blocking as before. This matches the finding's core concern about a backend outage/slow DB slowing/blocking anonymous authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When deviceLimit > 0, every anonymous request now issues an extra synchronous COUNT over the 30-day anon_device window before the upsert, doubling the DB round-trips on the authentication hot path, and the query's updated_at range predicate relies on an index on updated_at that this diff neither adds nor verifies. Every anonymous page load pays two DB queries (COUNT + UPDATE/INSERT) where one sufficed, and on a large anon_device table without an updated_at index the COUNT is a full scan per request — a scalability cliff exactly where the limit is configured (large anonymous deployments).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an extra DB round-trip on the anonymous auth path when a device limit is configured: `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` now calls `s.CountDevices(...)` over a ~30-day window before performing the upsert/update (`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`), and `Anonymous.Authenticate` now calls `TagDevice` synchronously (no goroutine/timeout) (`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`). This makes anonymous requests pay COUNT + UPDATE/INSERT where previously tagging was async and (typically) a single write. However, the claim about relying on an `updated_at` index is not verifiable from this diff (no schema/index context shown), so that part can’t be confirmed here. Overall this is a concrete scalability/perf concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration (30*24*time.Hour) is now duplicated as an identical constant in two packages (anonstore/database.go and anonimpl/api.go), replacing the previously shared thirtyDays with parallel hand-maintained copies. The device-limit window and the ListDevices window are semantically the same retention period but have no single source of truth; the next change to retention (e.g. 30d -> 7d) edits one file and silently makes the limit window disagree with the UI/API window, miscounting which devices count against the limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `const anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour` defined separately in two packages: `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` (used for device-limit counting and update window) and `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go` (used for `ListDevices` time range). They represent the same retention/window concept but are now parallel copies with no shared source of truth, so a future change could easily make the limit window and API/UI listing window diverge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Go DTO exposes AnonymousDeviceLimit as a plain int64 with no omitempty, so disabled (0) is serialized as 0, while the TS side models it as number | undefined and the runtime default is undefined — the two sides disagree on how 'no limit' is represented across the process boundary. Frontend code branching on undefined ('not configured') never sees it from the Go backend (always a number), and a frontend that treats 0 as 'limit of zero devices' rather than 'unlimited' misbehaves for every default-config deployment; the sentinel semantics are split between two type systems with no documented mapping.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real cross-boundary representation mismatch: Go always emits `anonymousDeviceLimit` as an `int64` field in `FrontendSettingsDTO` with no `omitempty` (so default `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` from `MustInt64(0)` will serialize as `0`), while the TS config models it as `number | undefined` and the runtime default is `undefined` (`GrafanaBootConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined`). That means the frontend will never observe `undefined` from the backend for default configs, only `0`. The finding’s claim about specific frontend branching/misbehavior isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, but the inconsistent sentinel semantics across Go/TS is directly evidenced by the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] device_limit is read with MustInt64 and consumed only via s.deviceLimit > 0, so negative values and the 0 default are silently equivalent to 'unlimited' with no validation or warning. An operator who sets device_limit = -1 (or makes a typo like device_limit = 1OO resolved to 0) gets unlimited anonymous devices with no log line, believing a limit is in force — the misconfiguration is invisible until the table grows unbounded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff reads `device_limit` via `anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)` into `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` and passes it to `ProvideAnonDBStore(..., cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)`. In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the limit is only enforced when `s.deviceLimit > 0`; otherwise (0 or negative) it behaves as unlimited, and there is no validation or log warning about non-positive values. That makes misconfiguration (e.g., negative) silently disable limiting, which is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case concern but not an outright functional defect in the implemented logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the device limit is reached, Authenticate returns (nil, ErrDeviceLimitReached), which fails the entire anonymous authentication instead of merely skipping device tagging, so every anonymous request from a new device is rejected once the limit is hit. Once device_limit is reached, all not-yet-seen anonymous devices get authentication errors on every request — the original intent was to cap tracked devices, not to deny anonymous access; the objective silently changed from 'limit device records' to 'lock out anonymous users' without human acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes anonymous authentication fail when device tagging hits the new limit. In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously and explicitly returns `(nil, err)` when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`. `TagDevice` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go` was also changed to return the error from `tagDeviceUI` instead of only logging it. In the store, when `deviceLimit > 0` and the count is >= limit, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls `updateDevice`, which returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` if no existing row was updated (i.e., a new device_id). This combination means once the limit is reached, any previously-unseen anonymous device will cause `Authenticate` to error on every request, effectively denying anonymous access rather than just skipping/limiting tracking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TagDevice now propagates tagDeviceUI errors (added 'return err') where it previously logged the failure and returned nil, so transient DB/cache failures now fail anonymous authentication. Any error from tagDeviceUI (DB blip, cache error) now turns into a failed anonymous authn request; previously such failures were degraded gracefully with a log line — a behavior change slipped in under a 'configurable device limit' PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show TagDevice now returns the error from tagDeviceUI (`return err` in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go), whereas previously it only logged. However, the finding’s core claim—that transient TagDevice/tagDeviceUI errors now fail anonymous authentication—is not supported by the diff: in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Authenticate only returns an error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`; all other TagDevice errors are logged (`a.log.Warn(...)`) and authentication continues by returning an Anonymous identity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Device tagging was silently converted from a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout and panic recovery to a synchronous inline call on the request path. Every anonymous request now pays the latency of a CountDevices query (and updateDevice insert) inline — a hot-path regression where a slow/degraded anonstore database directly delays all anonymous page loads, and a panic in TagDevice previously recovered no longer is contained.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change anonymous device tagging from async to synchronous on the request path: in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` the `go func(){...context.WithTimeout...recover...}` block was removed and replaced with an inline `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` call, so any latency/panic in tagging is no longer isolated. Also, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` now performs a `CountDevices(...)` query (and potentially an `UPDATE`) when `deviceLimit > 0`, which can add DB work to that path. However, the finding overstates that *every* anonymous request pays the CountDevices cost—it's conditional on `AnonymousDeviceLimit` being set > 0 (default is read as 0). This is a concrete perf/robustness regression concern, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateDevice's WHERE clause requires the existing device's updated_at to be within the 30-day window, so a known device whose row is older than 30 days gets ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being refreshed, permanently locking that returning device out even though it is a repeat visitor. A returning anonymous device with a stale row (e.g., rows not purged yet, or CreatedAt but stale updated_at) is treated as a new device and rejected every time; the device can never be re-admitted until DeleteDevicesOlderThan runs, defeating the intent of counting distinct devices.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, when the device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice() calls updateDevice(). updateDevice() only updates rows where `device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?`, with the bounds computed as `device.UpdatedAt - 30d` and `device.UpdatedAt + 1m`. If the existing device row’s `updated_at` is older than that 30-day window (e.g., stale record not yet deleted), the UPDATE affects 0 rows and the code returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. That makes a returning/known device unable to refresh its row under limit pressure, matching the finding’s described lockout behavior until cleanup occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The count-then-update limit check is a TOCTOU race: concurrent requests can each observe count < limit and insert, exceeding device_limit. Under concurrent anonymous traffic the limit is only approximate; operators configuring an exact cap get more devices than configured — acceptable if documented, but the config option reads as an exact guarantee.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the limit enforcement is implemented as `CountDevices(...)` followed by `if count >= s.deviceLimit { return s.updateDevice(...) }` else proceed to an insert/upsert path. There is no transaction/lock spanning the count and the subsequent insert, so concurrent requests can each observe `count < deviceLimit` and both insert new device IDs, exceeding the configured cap. This makes `device_limit` not strictly enforced under concurrency (a TOCTOU race) and is a correctness issue for a setting that reads like a hard limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts the injected anonStore.AnonStore and instead constructs AnonDBStore internally, removing the DI seam. Out-of-tree/enterprise code that injected a custom AnonStore implementation (e.g., a remote device store) silently stops being used; this is a public-surface change hidden inside a feature PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changed its signature from accepting an injected `anonstore.AnonStore` to accepting `sqlStore db.DB` and then constructing the store internally: `anonStore: anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go). This removes the DI seam for supplying an alternate `AnonStore` implementation. While not a runtime correctness defect inside this PR, it is a concrete architectural/public-surface change that can affect out-of-tree/enterprise integrations that previously injected a custom store.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The frontend type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined but the Go DTO serializes it as int64 with zero value 0, so the frontend can never observe 'undefined' and cannot distinguish 'unlimited' from a real limit of 0. Frontend code written against the declared type will treat the always-present 0 as a real value; anyone building UI/API surfacing on this field must know 0 means unset, a contract mismatch baked in at type level.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a contract/type mismatch: in TS `GrafanaConfig` declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` defaults it to `undefined`, but the backend DTO `FrontendSettingsDTO` defines `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"`` (no `omitempty`) and `getFrontendSettings` always assigns `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, which is read with `MustInt64(0)` in `readAuthSettings`. Therefore the JSON field will always be present (at least `0`), so the frontend cannot actually observe `undefined` and must implicitly treat `0` as “unset/unlimited”, contradicting the declared type and risking incorrect UI/logic written against it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit reuses the same Device struct and mutates DeviceID after the first insert, but the first device was inserted with UpdatedAt one hour in the past while the test's limit check counts devices within the 30-day window — the test only exercises the count>=limit path, never verifying that an existing device within the window can still be updated. The update path for an existing device when the limit is reached (the core intended behavior of the feature) has no coverage; a regression in the UPDATE matching would pass CI and lock out all returning devices in production.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`, the second call sets a new `DeviceID` ("keep") after the first insert, so when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` hits the `count >= s.deviceLimit` branch it calls `updateDevice` for a non-existent row and correctly gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (`rowsAffected == 0`). This test therefore only covers the "new device blocked when limit reached" behavior and does not cover the intended "existing (returning) device can still be updated when limit reached" path (i.e., `updateDevice` succeeding with `rowsAffected > 0`). That’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap in coverage, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices and then performs the upsert as two separate statements with no transaction or row lock, so concurrent anonymous requests all observe count < deviceLimit and each insert a new device row. Under concurrent load the configured device limit is exceeded (limit is advisory, not enforced), and conversely once near the limit concurrent requests race to return ErrDeviceLimitReached for devices that would have fit; an attacker driving parallel requests with rotating cookies can overshoot the operator's cap.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the device-limit enforcement does `CountDevices(...)` and then performs the insert/upsert as a separate operation with no surrounding transaction or locking. Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and all proceed to insert new rows, exceeding the configured limit. Conversely, near the limit, races can cause some requests to take the `count >= limit` path and return `ErrDeviceLimitReached` even though a slot may still be available at that moment. The diff shows no atomic DB constraint or transactional mechanism to prevent these races.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned from Authenticate as an authentication error, so anonymous requests from new devices surface as a generic auth failure (likely HTTP 500 from the authn pipeline) rather than a defined 4xx/redirect response, and the previously fire-and-forget tagging path is now a blocking failure point on every anonymous request. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A device whose stored updated_at is older than 30 days can never be updated once the limit is reached, because the UPDATE's `updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt-30d AND device.UpdatedAt+1m` window excludes it, RowsAffected returns 0, and the store permanently returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for that device. A returning anonymous user whose device row was last touched >30 days ago (it then stops being counted by CountDevices' 30-day window, so the limit appears to have room, yet the row still exists) is locked out forever: every request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and the row can never be refreshed back into the counted window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally enforces the 30-day “active device” window when the device limit is reached. In CreateOrUpdateDevice, ErrDeviceLimitReached can only happen when CountDevices(now-30d..now+1m) >= deviceLimit, in which case updateDevice only updates rows whose updated_at is within the last 30 days (relative to the incoming device.UpdatedAt, typically “now”). A device with updated_at older than 30 days is treated as expired/inactive; reactivating it would increase the active-count beyond the limit, so blocking it is consistent with the implemented policy. The finding’s key claim that the limit “appears to have room” because the old row isn’t counted is incorrect: if it isn’t counted, CountDevices would be lower and the code would take the normal upsert path (not updateDevice) and refresh the row successfully.

Under concurrency, multiple requests can all observe `count < deviceLimit` and each insert, exceeding the intended limit (classic TOCTOU). No code in the diff makes this atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Authenticate now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached as an authentication error, converting what was previously fire-and-forget device tagging into an authn failure that denies anonymous access to brand-new devices. Once the limit is reached, every new device gets an authentication failure (surfacing 'device limit reached' as the auth error) rather than anonymous access with an untagged device — a user-visible behavior change from the previous design where tagging failures never blocked authentication; if blocking is intended, the error message presented to end users is raw and unhelpful.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes device tagging part of the authn success path: `Anonymous.Authenticate` now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously and returns the error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `deviceLimit > 0` and the store already has `count >= deviceLimit`, and the device is new (update affects 0 rows) (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). This means once the limit is reached, a brand-new anonymous device causes `Authenticate` to fail, blocking anonymous access; previously tagging was done in a goroutine and failures only logged (fire-and-forget). The error is also a raw internal string (`fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")`) likely to surface as an unhelpful auth error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AnonymousDeviceLimit is added to FrontendSettingsDTO and GrafanaBootConfig but no code in this diff reads it on the frontend, and the TS default `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` never matches the Go serialization, which always emits the JSON number 0 for the unset case. Ships-inert frontend surface: the config field is broadcast to every browser on every page load carrying no consumer, and the `number | undefined` type misdescribes the actual wire shape (always a number, 0 meaning unset), so future frontend code checking truthiness will treat a legitimate limit of 0 (disabled) and 'absent' identically only by accident.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a wire/type mismatch: Go `FrontendSettingsDTO` adds `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` without `omitempty`, so JSON will always include a number (defaulting to `0` when unset), while the TS `GrafanaConfig` declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` initializes it to `undefined`. The finding’s point about the TS type not matching the serialized shape is grounded in the diff. However, the claim that “no code reads it on the frontend” and that it “ships inert frontend surface” cannot be verified from this diff alone (frontend usage could exist elsewhere), so it’s not provably a defect from the shown changes.
